headline: Googlebook event set for Sept. 15 with key questions about Aluminum OS and AI integration
summary: Google's media preview event for the Googlebook on September 15 will feature a keynote, OEM partner demos, and hands-on access. Key questions include the 'glowbar' functionality, Aluminum OS's Android/ChromeOS merger, and Gemini AI integration.
details: The Googlebook media preview event is officially scheduled for September 15 in New York, according to Chrome Unboxed. The event will feature a keynote from Google leadership, OEM partner demo stations, and hands-on access for media.

This announcement follows the Made by Google event, where the Googlebook was only briefly mentioned as a 'Chromebook replacement' coming this fall. Partners like Asus, HP, and Lenovo are expected to be involved.

One major question revolves around the 'glowbar,' a multi-colored LED light strip on the Googlebook's lid, which Google describes as 'functional and beautiful.' It's speculated to act as a notification bar, similar to the Pixel 11 series' HiLight.

Another key area is Aluminum OS, built on Android 17, designed to merge Android and ChromeOS for smoother integration and multitasking between devices. Its success in unifying the two platforms will be closely watched.
AI integration, with Gemini as the centerpiece, is also a focus, despite past resistance in Google Home and Android Auto. Its role and user acceptance in the Googlebook ecosystem remain to be seen.

Finally, the Googlebook's impact on Google's education market, currently dominated by Chromebooks, is a concern. With its reportedly premium materials, it faces competition from budget-friendly options like the MacBook Neo.

headline_marked: [[ICE agents banned from wearing Meta glasses]] at work, official memo warns
headline: ICE agents banned from wearing Meta glasses at work, official memo warns
summary: A new memo from Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) prohibits employees from using Meta glasses due to privacy and legal concerns. This clarifies an existing policy against personal body-worn cameras.
details: Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has issued a memo banning its employees from wearing Meta glasses or similar devices during work. The agency states that these devices could "unintentionally capture, record, or transmit sensitive information," potentially compromising privacy and legal protections.

This policy applies to all ICE employees, not just field agents, and clarifies an existing Department of Homeland Security (DHS) rule against personally owned body-worn cameras. The memo highlights the increasing visibility of Meta's smart glasses amidst US immigration crackdowns.

Despite the policy, ICE and Customs and Border Patrol (CBP) agents have been repeatedly seen wearing Meta smart glasses in recent months. Reports include a CBP agent recording with his glasses and another wearing a pair during an immigration raid in at least six states.

Interestingly, while banning personal smart glasses, DHS is reportedly exploring official versions of the technology for its officers. Budget documents suggest ICE aims to equip its personnel with bespoke smart glasses featuring "biometric identification capabilities" by next year.

Meta has not publicly commented on its products' suitability for law enforcement, but an association with ICE could fuel ongoing backlash. The company faces privacy concerns over an unreleased facial recognition feature and the ease with which the glasses' privacy-protecting LED can be bypassed.
